sources: dossier=Net position (root module layered foundation→graph→runtime→control) + Required behaviors (depguard layer ordering); doc=graph/runtime/control layer sub-bullets were indented as children of the Examples-module bullet, describing layers that belong to the Root-module bullet immediately above them; code=n/a, this is an internal doc-structure defect verifiable from the doc's own prose (Root-module bullet text names these three layers, Examples-module bullet describes an unrelated reference-impl surface)

sources: dossier=Net position ('root module is layered foundation → graph → runtime → control') + doc's own Invariants ('Layer ordering: foundation → graph → runtime → control'); doc=line 12 parenthetical named only graph+runtime+control while calling it a four-layer split; code=n/a

sources: dossier=Net position (foundation is a separate go.work module, self-contained, no replace directive against root) corroborated by go.work listing lib/foundation as its own `use` entry distinct from root; doc=Purpose and Boundaries both said 'the four-layer ordering inside the root module's library code', but the doc's own Foundation-module bullet places foundation as a sibling module, not inside root (Root-module bullet enumerates only graph/runtime/control)
note: The four-layer ordering spans two Go modules (foundation module + root module's graph/runtime/control), not one. Reworded both occurrences to 'spanning the foundation and root modules' library code' instead of claiming containment in the root module alone.

sources: dossier=silent on this specific sentence, but corroborated independently by CLAUDE.md ('Backend (postgres|sqlite) is selected by config') and the concept doc's own Foundation-module bullet and Invariants bullet, both of which pin a pure-Go SQLite driver as a first-class supported backend; doc=Invariants line said 'cross-process state flows through Postgres only', an absolute claim inconsistent with the doc's own dual-backend treatment two bullets earlier; code=not consulted (not needed; contradiction is doc-internal plus corroborated by CLAUDE.md)

sources: dossier=n/a (style rule, not an intent question); doc=Services-module bullet used 'the new edge is one-way (cmd → services)', changelog-voice phrasing; authority=.ok-planner/CLAUDE.md current-state-only rule (no 'previously'/'new'/dated framing in design-doc prose), an enforcement surface for the design corpus itself

sources: dossier=Net position ('lib/services is its own module requiring only lib/protocols, so the module graph itself enforces consumption-side isolation', 2026-05-27, artifact) — now superseded by fact; corroborated independently by (a) lib/services/go.mod's actual require block, which lists the root module and lib/foundation alongside lib/protocols, and (b) .golangci.yml's own consumption-side-isolation comment, which documents that the lib/services/test/ tree legitimately imports cmd/rimsky/cli for CLICTRL acceptance scenarios and is exempted from the package-level deny rule; doc=Invariants line 42 claimed 'the module graph reinforces the same boundary... the services module requires only the protocols module'
note: go.mod now requires root+foundation (for the module's own out-of-tree test tree); the module graph no longer excludes rimsky-internal layers on its own. Enforcement is single (the depguard lint rule). Dropped the false module-graph clause from the Invariants bullet and stated single enforcement plus the reason (test-only requires).

sources: dossier=same Net-position entry as row 511, same supersession; corroborated by the same lib/services/go.mod require block and .golangci.yml comment; doc=Services-module bullet (line 16) repeated both the 'Depends only on the protocols module' claim and the 'enforced twice: by the module graph...' claim
note: Same underlying defect as row 511 (module-graph-enforcement claim is now false), restated at a second site in the Purpose-section module bullet rather than the Invariants bullet — a distinct edit location, not a no-op duplicate. Rewrote the bullet to distinguish the shipped bundled-service packages (protocols-only) from the module's manifest (also requires root+foundation for its own test tree), and to state single (lint-only) enforcement.

sources: dossier=Net position ('examples module... protocols-only', 2026-06-08, corpus-bootstrap, artifact-only) — accurate for the published surface but silent on the test-only exception; corroborated by examples/go.mod's own require block (direct require on lib/services) and its own inline rationale comment, which states the test-only dependency never reaches consumers who `go build` the examples normally; doc=Examples-module bullet (line 18) and Licensing-boundary 'closed permissive island' sentence (line 51) both said examples imports only the protocols module, with no qualification
note: The shipped/go-build surface is genuinely protocols-only (matches the licensing-boundary invariant), but the module's own manifest carries a direct test-only dependency on the services module for a cross-stack e2e proof. Qualified both sentences to distinguish the published surface (protocols-only, preserving the permissive-island claim) from the module's test-only dependency (never ships).
